chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Shadhan al-Naysaburi, who said:

Five hundred dirhams less twenty dirhams had been gathered with me, and I disliked sending five hundred dirhams less twenty dirhams. So I weighed out twenty dirhams from my own possession and sent them to al-Asadi, and I did not write what belonged to me in it. Then there came: 'Five hundred dirhams have arrived; twenty dirhams of them are yours.'

key_terms.الْأَسَدِيِّ: al-Asadi, the person to whom the money was sent
key_terms.خَمْسُمِائَةِ دِرْهَمٍ: a sum of five hundred dirhams
key_terms.عِشْرِينَ دِرْهَمًا: twenty dirhams added from the sender's own money
key_terms.فَأَنِفْتُ: I felt aversion or disdained doing so
key_terms.وَلَمْ أَكْتُبْ: I did not write or specify

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith show the Imam's knowledge of a concealed financial detail?
ai.summary: This report narrates that Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Shadhan al-Naysaburi added twenty dirhams of his own money to complete a sum before sending it onward. A reply then accurately identified that twenty dirhams in the amount belonged to him, demonstrating precise knowledge of what had been sent.
